items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I first arrived in New York, I worked with the Hot Lips Page Group.

ctx.x: Did Lucky Thompson have—Was he how you got to Hot Lips Page?

Lucky had worked with Lips before I got there. As a matter of fact, Lucky sent me a letter saying that Lips needed a pianist. He said that he needed a pianist within a certain length of time, let's say a year. So, within that year, I took the time to go to Cleveland to work at a place called Cedar Gardens for a while. After this Cedar Gardens I went to Buffalo to work at a bar. After that bar, I went to New York and joined Lips Page at that Onyx Club. This was after getting permission from the union to work on a…
What was the situation like in Buffalo?

items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I first arrived in New York, I worked with the Hot Lips Page Group... Of course, we played his style.

ctx.x: Okay, I want to switch gears and I want to go to 52nd street. I want to go to when you arrived in New York. I want you to describe the band that you came into, and the performance circumstance that you came into that was 52nd St. in 1944 or 43.

It was 1943. And might have been 1946. Because, I saw Jazz with the Philharmonic in 1946. So, prior to that I had worked on the street for some time. When I first arrived in New York, I worked with the Hot Lips Page Group. We had Buford Oliver playing drums. Karl "Flat Top” Wilson playing bass, and of course Hot Lips Page playing trumpet. For a while, there was a guitar player, I don't remember his name. Of course, we played his style. His trumpet style was similar to a Louis Armstrong style. In a way, I think…
Had you done boogie-woogie before? That’s like Albert Ammons and that stuff.
